title: Successor freeze candidate: close S1 stored XSS and S2 final-lock database integrity
owner_ruling: FIX BOTH BEFORE PARTICIPANT USE. Neither risk accepted for the study period.

S1.title: stored XSS / content-type spoofing on GET /documents/{id}/content
S1.reproduction_before_fix: Re-reproduced on current v25 rather than taken from the Run-40 artifact. The client-supplied mimeType is stored verbatim at upload and echoed as the response Content-Type with Content-Disposition: inline and no nosniff. In real Chromium, loading the route in a same-origin iframe exactly as assets/js/files.js previews documents, 4 of 4 attacker payloads (text/html under a .pdf name, .html, image/svg+xml, and a stored-MIME mismatch) reached the boundary at HTTP 200 and EXECUTED script in the application origin.
S1.remediation: server/app/main.py: Content-Type drawn from a server-controlled inline-safe allowlist (application/pdf, png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp, text/plain); everything else, including text/html, image/svg+xml, xhtml and xml, served as application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition: attachment; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response; Content-Disposition filename sanitised against quotes, backslashes and control characters. Reuses the implementation proven in commit a3fd8b6, reconstructed and re-checked against current main first. Stored bytes, authorization, extraction and evidence meaning untouched.
S1.result_after_fix: 0 of 4 attacker payloads execute; all 4 still reach the serving boundary at HTTP 200, so the refusal is this boundary's and not an unrelated gate's. Legitimate PDF and text documents still serve inline with bytes unchanged.
S1.intended_functional_consequence: image/svg+xml is script-capable and is now downloaded rather than rendered inline. Retrieval still works; only in-place SVG rendering changes.

S2.title: final-lock database integrity on the primary outcome data
S2.reproduction_before_fix: Reproduced on the v25 schema in an isolated SQLite with the decision driven to final lock entirely through the real application routes (researchevidenceget -> researchprejudgment -> researchreveal -> researchdecision). With final_submitted_at set, 13 of 13 direct raw-SQL UPDATEs succeeded, rewriting every substantive final-response field and clearing final_submitted_at itself.
S2.remediation: Migration 0026 adds trg_decisions_final_lock_guard, mirroring migration 0003's preliminary-lock guard onto the final side, on Postgres (plpgsql, SQLSTATE OG002) and SQLite.
S2.protected_field_set_derivation: DERIVED MECHANICALLY, NOT TAKEN FROM THE PROMPT. server/tools/run41_derive_final_fields.py reads the AST of a_researchdecision, the only route that records a final response, and cross-checks every decision.<attr> assignment against EXPORT_COLUMNS in research_export.py. Both authorities agree on the same 13 names.
S2.discrepancy_with_prompt: The owner's prompt named 3 fields (final_action, final_confidence, rationale). The live model has 12 substantive final-response fields. The 9 the prompt did not name are disposition (the participant's stance toward the AI recommendation), evidence_items (evidence use), reason_code, escalation_level, owner_role, authority_role, resource_constraint, deadline and residual_risk. All 12 are analysis-export variables. Protecting only the named 3 would have left 9 components of the primary outcome editable. Reported rather than absorbed.
S2.lock_timestamp_also_protected: final_submitted_at is protected as a 13th column because it is the guard's own predicate; a trigger keyed off a timestamp it permits to be cleared is bypassable in two statements.
S2.predeclared_idempotent_write: PERMITTED. An UPDATE setting a protected field to the value it already holds is allowed, matching trg_decisions_pre_lock_guard's IS DISTINCT FROM semantics: the guard exists to stop the final response CHANGING, and refusing a write that changes nothing would break ordinary ORM flushes and obstruct normal operation, which section 7 forbids.
S2.result_after_fix: 0 of 13 raw-SQL mutations succeed after final lock. Every attack proved to reach the trigger: the identical UPDATE is run on a control decision stopped just before the final lock, where 13 of 13 SUCCEED, so the post-lock refusal is the lock state and nothing else. Pre-lock writes, unprotected columns, reads, sessions, reload and export are unaffected.
